The text exhibits sarcasm in the statement "Nothing pleases me more than standing in a long queue at the post office. It's such an efficient use of my time." The speaker claims to enjoy a universally disliked experience (waiting in long lines) and describes it as "efficient," which is the opposite of the typical negative sentiment associated with wasting time in queues. This ironic contrast flips the literal meaning, creating a negative sentiment polarity where the speaker is actually expressing frustration or annoyance.
